verification_report.summary:
The complete submitted proof is correct under the stipulated accepted prerequisites. Ten sequential records verify 47 deductions, and four reference records check the external attribution and prerequisite applications. No critical error or gap was found.

Local comparison: Lelong monotonicity gives α_i+β_i≥c_i, so a_i=min(α_i,c_i), b_i=c_i-a_i is an admissible split. Local smooth corrections make Siu decomposition applicable; the residual potentials are bounded above on smaller charts. With the book's weight exp(-mu) and logarithms log|z|², radial integrability gives ord_Ei(f∘π)+A_i>ma_i, where A_i=ord_Ei(Jac π)+1. Applying this to both factors yields ord_Ei((fg)∘π)>mc_i-2A_i, with exactly the printed normalization.

Monomial division and descent: choose C≥max_i(2A_i/c_i), m>C, and N_i=max(0,floor(mc_i-2A_i)+1). Each product generator is divisible by the integer monomial Πz_i^N_i, including at divisor intersections, and N_i≥(m-C)c_i. Bounded holomorphic quotients and the identity Σ|f_j|²Σ|g_l|²=Σ|f_jg_l|² give the asserted ordinary comparison. Proper inverse images of compactly contained downstairs sets admit finite covers, so the bounded constants can be maximized and the inequality descends by surjectivity. A finite downstairs cover gives one C independent of m; bounded errors may depend on m. Empty divisors cause no problem. Local resolutions suffice, without globalizing local modifications or descending quotient functions.

Trace equality: u+v also has zero generic Lelong number along Y. The accepted exact analytic approximants therefore have genuine restrictions of the stated image-ideal types. Restricting the ordinary inequality, pulling back to any fixed smooth compact modification, and taking generic Lelong numbers gives the displayed order inequality in the correct direction. Fix k first; the comparison constants may depend on k. The finite integer profile limits let m tend to infinity, giving τ_u+τ_v≥ord_E(a_k(u+v;Y))/k. Then k tends to infinity, proving the reverse of the accepted subadditivity inequality and hence exact equality. Bounded errors disappear before either limit.

Curves: coefficient equality gives D_(u+v)=D_u+D_v as finite positive atomic measures. A common nonpositive Green kernel makes the corresponding potentials add pointwise, including poles; the accepted uniform L1 bound ensures genuine representatives. Their established ordinary-type independence proves the claimed ordinary singularity-type addition. Positive real homogeneity follows by the same integral argument from the full real-parameter profile homogeneity. No equality for maxima is asserted.

Reference audit: arXiv theorem search was followed by web verification and a complete reading of the local published Cao text, with visual inspection of pages 118–119. Theorem 1.4 and its resolution argument match the attribution. Cao's singularity order is opposite to the book's, and his printed Bergman coefficient paired with exp(-2kφ) has the flagged factor mismatch. That formula and his global closed-positive-current theorem are not imported; the submitted calculation is verified independently. [Cao, published paper](https://www.numdam.org/item/CRMATH_2015__353_2_117_0.pdf).

All three accepted prerequisite reports were read. The curve metric supplement is not needed for this new argument. No BMP, global closed positive background, Monge–Ampère mass convergence, ambient singularity metric, or novelty claim is used. The book was left unchanged.
